headline: Every major above its 200-day and every RSI overbought at once
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it is unusually clean today: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB and DOGE all sit above their 200-day line, only ADA sits below it after a 75.7% drawdown from its 12-month high. Six of seven majors agreeing on trend direction is not the norm, it is the kind of alignment you see when a rally has been running long enough to drag the slow average up with it. BTC itself is still 38.2% off its 12-month high of $124,739, so this is a recovery within a larger drawdown, not a fresh all-time-high melt-up.

Momentum is where the story turns interesting. Every asset in the set is technically overbought: SOL at RSI 82.0, XRP at 86.0, BNB at 83.8, DOGE at 81.8, BTC itself at 80.4. MACD lines sit above signal across the board, so trend and momentum agree for now, there's no bearish divergence forming yet. But RSI north of 80 on six different assets simultaneously is stretched by any desk's definition, the kind of reading that usually precedes a cooling-off period even if the direction of that cooldown isn't something the chart tells you in advance. BTC's 24h print of -1.55% and ETH's -3.83% look like the first flex of that stretch, both still up over 20% and nearly 29% respectively over the past 7 days.

Positioning adds a wrinkle rather than a warning. BTC funding on OKX sits at 0.01% per 8 hours (about 11% annualized), which is mild, not the kind of expensive, crowded long book that precedes a violent unwind. But the long/short account ratios tell a different story down the cap table: DOGE traders are long at 3.29 to 1, SOL at 2.19 to 1, XRP at 1.56 to 1. That's a crowd leaning hard into the smaller, more volatile names while BTC's book stays closer to balanced at 1.13. Liquidations in the last few hours skew heavily toward longs getting flushed: BTC longs lost $14.1M against $3.2M in shorts, ETH longs $20.5M against $4.2M in shorts. Leverage is getting tested on the long side even as price holds up.

Flows are where the tension sharpens. US spot ETFs printed net inflows on Aug 21, $307.5M into BTC funds and $184.0M into ETH funds, both five-day runs positive (same_direction_days of 5, with $1.92B and $692.6M respectively over that window), a real, sustained traditional-finance bid. But whale wallets are doing the opposite in the last 24 hours: $160.3M net moved onto exchanges, with ETH alone seeing $161.6M land on Coinbase Institutional and other venues (BTC actually saw a small $1.4M net move off exchanges, so this is an ETH-specific push). Zoom out to the weekly view and the pattern has flipped in the past two weeks: after weeks of $922M and $484M moving off exchanges (late July into early August), the last two weeks ending Aug 15 and Aug 22 both show net inflows onto exchanges, $573M and $553M. Coins are quietly finding their way back to venues where they can be sold, even as the ETF wrapper keeps buying.

Sentiment sits at 71, Greed, near the top of its own 30-day range of 25 to 72. It agrees with the price action but not fully with the whale ledger: a crowd feeling good while size moves onto exchanges is worth flagging, it's not necessarily bearish, exchange balances can rise for lots of reasons, but it's the kind of divergence that matters more than the mood ring itself. Stablecoin float is essentially flat over 30 days (+0.26% to $308.5B), so the dry powder on the sidelines isn't growing, it's just sitting.

What to watch from here: whether the two-week trend of net inflows onto exchanges extends into a third week or reverses, whether ETF net flows hold their five-day positive streak or break it, and whether the long/short ratios on SOL, XRP and DOGE unwind through the exchange's liquidation engine or through an orderly rotation. A funding flip negative on BTC while RSI stays elevated would also be a signal worth naming when and if it shows up.
